name: Papua New Guinea Mile High A, Eastern Highlands
origin: Papua New Guinea, Eastern Highlands, Kainantu (Arokara Cooperative)
vendor_notes: Bright acidity and creamy body with berries, caramel, malt and citrus. Brightness 6/7.
goal: Light roast: bright berry and citrus with caramel sweetness
rationale: A clean washed coffee from 1,600 m with old Typica/Bourbon lines: fairly dense, takes heat well, and its berry and citrus acidity is the point, so it gets a light roast: DTR ~18% and ~9.5 C after first crack. A solid start (charge 190 C) keeps momentum so the roast doesn't stall and taste flat, and burner steps begin ~2 min before FC so RoR is ~8 at crack and falling. If it tastes sour or thin, add 10-15 s of development.
steps: Preheat to 190 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 190. Burner 73%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:42 near 103 C. RoR peaks around 1:30.
At 178 C (~6:09): burner 46%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:15 at ~188 C: burner 41%, air 50. Then 36%.
Drop ~8:50 at ~197.5 C (9.5 C after FC).

history.note: Initial plan (for a family member) from the Coffee Bean Corral page and the 2026-09-29 calibration: TP ~0:40, Honduras FC 188.9 C, burner steps ~2 min before FC.
